newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's leader to visit Washington in May.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's leader to visit Washington in May.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma is due to visit the United States in the middle of May to discuss relations between Kiev and NATO, and boost political and business ties, a presidential spokesman said on Tuesday.
Kuchma will hold talks with President Bill Clinton and will chair with U.S. Vice-President Albert Gore a meeting of the Ukrainian-American committee on economic cooperation.
Sources within the presidential administration said Kuchma would begin his visit on May 16.
Kiev considers Washington a strategic partner, and Ukraine is the third largest recepient of U.S. foreign aid after Egypt and Israel.
Unlike Russia, Ukraine does not oppose future enlargement of NATO, but it has not formally applied for membership.
Diplomats have suggested a document on Kiev's relationship with NATO would be signed at the alliance's July Madrid summit.
